title: Trunk and trunk-subsegment masses (UPT/MPT/LPT), male and female

quantity.name: segment mass
quantity.definition: segment mass relative to body mass

source.n: 115 subjects (100 M, 15 F) – secondary analysis of Zatsiorsky et al. gamma-ray scanning data
source.sample: college-aged Caucasian living subjects, mostly physical-education undergraduates (Zatsiorsky et al. 1990a,b, 1993)
source.notes: Reference subject in Table 4: F body mass 61.9 kg, stature 1.735 m (printed '173.5 m'); M 73.0 kg, 1.741 m. DOI not printed in PDF (standard citation; verify).

protocol.summary: Adjusted Zatsiorsky–Seluyanov segment parameters: trunk and its three parts.
how_to_use: Assign UPT/MPT/LPT = 15.96/16.33/11.17 % BM (male) or 15.45/14.65/12.47 % BM (female); whole trunk 43.46 % (M) / 42.57 % (F).
UPT ends at xyphion (~T9), MPT at omphalion (~L3/L4), LPT at the hip-joint-centre midpoint – map these to vertebral levels before lumping onto a spine model.
Head+neck (6.94/6.68 %) and arms are separate segments; add them to the upper trunk load if the model has no arms.

measurement.method: gamma-ray scanning (original Zatsiorsky data), re-referenced to joint centres using anthropometric surveys
measurement.posture: standing/supine scanning (original); parameters for anatomical position

protocol.notes: Landmarks: SUPR suprasternale, XYPH xyphion, OMPH omphalion (navel), MIDH mid-point of hip joint centres, MIDS mid-point of shoulder joint centres, CERV cervicale (C7 spinous process), VERT vertex, MIDG mid-gonion. UPT=SUPR-XYPH, MPT=XYPH-OMPH, LPT=OMPH-MIDH (close to Pearsall 1994 thorax/abdomen/pelvis landmark boundaries, but Pearsall's thorax starts at the suprasternal notch and pelvis ends at pubis/trochanter).

extraction.check_notes: All values re-read from the rotated 200-dpi image of Table 4 (p.1228). Corrected OCR: alternative 'Trunk MIDS-MIDH' female mass is 42.57 (OCR 42.51). Values marked * in the paper (MPT, Foot, Head VERT-CERV, UPT CERV-XYPH, Hand STYL-DAC3) are not adjusted ('adjusted': false). Table 4 caption prints female stature '173.5 m' (should be 1.735 m). No erratum included in the PDF.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
